title: scheduler-backpressure-admission-control
content:
Summary:
This is a working design doc for scheduler-level backpressure and admission control in the serving runtime. Covers: queueing tiers, timeouts, admission policies (token-bucket/leaky-bucket), per-tenant limits, eviction semantics for KV cache hot-keys, and how backpressure signals flow to upstream proxies and SDKs.

Goals:
- Prevent tail-latency amplification under overload while preserving throughput for healthy tenants.
- Provide predictable SLOs via per-tenant and global admission controls.
- Allow graceful degradation (soft-fail, queuing, fallback model) rather than hard failures where possible.
- Surface clear metrics/alerts to SRE and product teams.

Non-goals:
- Full rate limiting for business quotas (billing layer handles hard quota enforcement).
- Replacing edge/API gateway rate limits — this complements them at the scheduler level.

Constraints & Assumptions:
- Instances handle batches of requests (continuous batching). Admission must be cheap (O(1) per request).
- Requests vary in cost: short completions (chat) vs long generations; admission should consider estimated token budget.
- Multi-tenant: tenants have different commitments (best-effort, reserved/dedicated).
- KV cache access may cause additional CPU/GPU memory pressure; admission should account for cache pressure signals.

Terminology:
- Tenant: customer account.
- Request cost: estimated GPU compute units (based on sequence length + model profile).
- Soft timeout: time after which request should be returned with a degrade/fallback.
- Hard timeout: abort and free resources.

Design overview (high level):
1) Admission layers (fast path):
   - Pre-queue admission: quick token-bucket checks at front-end scheduler to decide immediate accept / short-queue / reject. Cheap counters per tenant + global.
   - Priority queues: multiple queues per scheduler worker: reserved, standard, background. Each queue has separate configuration for max depth and dequeue policy.
   - Batch formation: admitted requests sit in per-queue ready lists for batching windows. If batch triggers, we dispatch.

2) Backpressure signals and inputs:
   - Internal: per-worker queue length, average batch latency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit/miss rate, memory pressure.
   - Upstream: API gateway rejection rate, client-side retry patterns.
   - External policy: per-tenant SLA level (reserved vs best-effort).

3) Admission algorithm details:
   - Per-tenant token bucket where tokens represent compute units. Tokens refill at tenant.rate (compute units/sec). Request consumes token = ceil(estimated_cost / token_unit). If insufficient tokens -> two options: enqueue to soft-queue (if queue depth allowed) OR reject.
   - Global safety bucket to absorb bursts; when depleted, we tighten admission across all best-effort tenants.
   - Priority preemption: reserved traffic bypasses best-effort queues up to a hard floor.
   - Dynamic scaling: when average batch lead-time > lead_time_threshold OR GPU utilization > util_threshold, reduce refill rates for best-effort tenants by multiplicative factor (0.5) until metrics recover.

4) Queueing and timeout semantics:
   - Each admitted request stamped with: arrival_ts, soft_deadline = arrival_ts + soft_timeout, hard_deadline = arrival_ts + hard_timeout.
   - If request waits beyond soft_deadline -> trigger degrade callback: fallback model invocation, cached response, or partial result. This is configurable per-route.
   - If wait beyond hard_deadline -> abort from queue and return explicit error with telemetry for diagnosis.

5) KV cache interplay:
   - Cache hotkey pressure tracked as an independent signal. If cache miss latencies increase or eviction churn high, favor requests with high predicted reuse (e.g., same conversation).
   - Requests that would warm the cache (prefix-heavy) may be deprioritized under severe memory pressure to avoid eviction storms.

Admission policy examples:
- Tenant A (reserved): high refill rate, large per-tenant queue, bypass to reserved queue.
- Tenant B (freemium): low refill rate, small queue, aggressive soft-timeout -> early fallback to smaller model.

Metrics to expose (per-tenant + global):
- admitted_count, rejected_count, enqueue_count, dequeue_count, avg_queue_time_p50/p90/p99, token_bucket_fill, token_consumed, gpu_utilization, kv_eviction_rate, fallback_invocations, hard_timeout_aborts.

Observability / Tracing:
- Every request carries admission trace: {precheck,result,queue_ts,dispatch_ts,dispatch_batch_id,reason_for_reject}. Store as trace tags and surface in Console (per-route).
- Alerting: sustained p95 queue time > X for > 5m, or hard_timeout_aborts > threshold.

Config knobs (operator-controlled):
- tenant.refill_rate, tenant.bucket_size, tenant.queue_depth, tenant.soft_timeout_ms, tenant.hard_timeout_ms, tenant.priority_class.
- global.util_threshold, global.global_bucket_size, global.scaling_factor_on_pressure.

Failure and rollout plan:
- Start as dry-run: only log what would have been rejected or downgraded for 2 weeks.
- Canary small fraction of clusters with enforcement for best-effort tenants.
- Gradually expand and tune thresholds with SRE.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for token bucket semantics and queue eviction.
- Load tests: synthetic multi-tenant workloads with mixed request costs to validate p99 latency under overload.
- Chaos: inject high KV eviction churn and verify degradations occur as designed.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How to estimate request cost precisely at admission time? (we currently use model profile + prompt length; need to include dynamic reply-length estimate)
- Interaction with autoscaling: should admission relax during scale-up warm-up? Probably yes but needs safety floor.
- Cross-worker fairness: tokens are per-tenant but requests routed to many workers; need consistent hashing or token sync. Simple approach: allocate tenant tokens per worker proportionally to expected load with periodic rebalance.

TODOs:
- [ ] Prototype token-bucket + queue in local scheduler (PR #789 exists with scaffolding).
- [ ] Add KV pressure metric emitters in cache layer. (owner: Liu Wei)
- [ ] Build Console dashboard for admission metrics (owner: Miguel).
- [ ] Draft SDK guidance for client-side retry/backoff when receiving soft rejects.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic. Focus review feedback on: missing signals, potential for tight feedback loops, and extreme corner cases (burst storms, flash crowd).
- If we add admission decisions that require cross-worker coordination, cost/latency might increase — prefer conservative per-worker heuristics first.

References:
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789
- Jira: JIRA-RES-312 (scheduler admission epic)
